To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The attachment of HeLA cells to a glass substrate is a function of the negative charge and the amount of Na + in that glass surface; 2) The amount of charge and the amount Na + required for attachment are greater than that characteristic for untreated glass; 3) A method for treating a soft-glass surface to produce the required properties was developed; 4) The treated surfaces were found to support attachment and growth of HeLa cells in protein free synthetic medium;
the attachment of HeLa (strain S-3Y) cells to glass is a function of total negative charge, amount of sodium in glass, and possibly other properties.
the growth of cells in a protein-free medium requires the presence of a surface with specific properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical and chemical requirements for attachment of HeLa cell to a surface in the absence of a proteinaceous coating.
the development of methods for the cultivation of mammalian cells, in a protein-free, synthetic medium.
the development of synthetic media for the cultivation of mammalian cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the physical properties of a glass surface are important in determining its ability to support the growth of mammalian tissue cells in synthetic medium, and the method of preparation of the glass surface is of equal importance.

the attachment of HeLa S-3Y cells in a protein free, synthetic medium is a function of two properties of the glass used for cultivation; the total amount of sodium, and the total negative charge on the surface.
the physical properties of the surface of the culture vessels used for cultivation of mammalian cells are of primary importance in determining the growth of cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the growth of mammalian tissue cells in protein free media can be accomplished by the use of specially prepared glass surfaces.

a surface of glass with an appropriate charge density, and sodium ion concentration is capable of supporting the attachment and growth in a protein free medium of a population of cells which has been adapted to grow in a protein free environment.
a protein free synthetic nutrient can be used to cultivate HeLa cells in the absence, or presence of protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface charge and the sodium content of a glass surface are the two most important properties of the glass for the attachment of mammalian cells.

the attachment and growth properties of HeLa cells are dependent on the physical properties of the substrate surface, and that the physical properties of a glass substrate surface can be altered in order to promote attachment of the cells.
the glass surface must be modified in a certain way to support cell growth in a protein-free synthetic medium.
